headline: Rent increases approved for 131 Sherman Street and 439 Conger Street; 90 Pine Street approved at $75.80; 117 Preble Street tabled.
summary: The meeting approved rent increase applications for 131 Sherman Street, 439 Conger Street, and 90 Pine Street. It tabled the application for 117 Preble Street until more information is received. It also approved several findings, changes to the public access rule, and a tentative November meeting date.
decisions: Approved, 4-0, findings of fact and conclusions of law for 24 Row Avenue, units one and two.
Approved, 4-0, findings of fact and conclusions of law for 56 and 58 Federal Street.
Approved, 4-0, findings of fact and conclusions of law for 341 Cumberland Ave., all 29 units.
Approved, 4-0, removing $10,361 in legal fees from the 439 Conger Street expenses because the cost does not recur year to year.
Approved, 4-0, rent increase application for 439 Conger Street, all 81 units, at $7.98.
Approved, 4-0, changes to Article 11 of the rent board's rules of procedure on public access to applications and materials.
Found complete, 4-0, the application for 91 State Street, pending more information on normal repairs.
Tabled, 4-0, the application for 117 Preble Street until more detailed information is received.
Approved, 4-0, rent increase application for 90 Pine Street of $75.80 for all four units.
Approved, 4-0, treating the $7,081.22 change in turnover expense as a capital improvement for unit six, amortized over five years.
Approved, 4-0, striking $1,381.22 in 2022 legal fees from the 131 Sherman Street application as a one-time expense.
Approved, 4-0, using the 2021 water and sewer cost increased by 3.7% in place of the 2022 figure for 131 Sherman Street.
Approved, 4-0, rent increase for 131 Sherman Street: $50.69 for units one through five and $168.71 for unit six.
Approved, 4-0, tentatively moving the November regular meeting to November 18 at 5 p.m. Eastern time.
discussion: Unit six turnover costs: Members discussed whether cleaning and repair costs after one long tenancy were one-time or capital costs, and agreed to spread them over five years for that unit only.
Unit six water costs: Members said the water spike tied to one tenancy did not reflect yearly costs, so the board used the 2021 water and sewer figure increased by 3.7%.

131 Sherman public comment: Objectors said the increase came mostly from one unit's turnover, legal, and water costs, and asked the board to deny it. The applicant said the costs were legitimate housing costs.
439 Conger legal fees: Members questioned whether a $10,361 legal cost tied to one human rights matter fits regular yearly costs, and removed it.
117 Preble information requests: Members asked for more detail on utility, insurance, cleaning, security, and HVAC costs, and on the number of units, before the application moves forward.
